answer: Attention Residue Ledger. Each identity must leave a continuous trace of low-value interactions that wander across unrelated tasks over days, and a scored window rejects identities whose activity fails to ripple into later independent sessions. An attacker must staff each fake identity with sustained, non-repetitive attention; the ember of activity must persist past the scoring cutoff or the identity is dropped. This costs roughly forty hours of genuine distributed engagement per identity to survive one review cycle, making farms economically unviable.
